newsitem.title: UK: British farmers welcome EU beef aid package.
newsitem.headline: British farmers welcome EU beef aid package.

text.p: British beef farmers welcomed the extra aid package provided to them after a meeting between European Union (EU) farm ministers in Luxembourg on Wednesday.
David Naish, president of Britain's National Farmers' Union (NFU), said in a statement on Thursday the deal should bring much needed additional help to beleaguered beef farmers.
"The extra 50 million is very welcome news. The NFU will be giving very close and lengthy consideration as to how this extra money should be spent," Naish said in a statement.
But he stressed that the European Commission now needed to make the renegotiation of the European beef regime a priority.
Naish said the package alleviated many of the short-term problems in the beef sector, but farmers now needed to make a long-term view of the market.
France, Germany and Britain were given half of the total 500 million Ecu aid the EU decided to extend to farmers hurt by the mad cow crisis and to cut beef surpluses.
The aid supplemented the 850 million Ecus package agreed by EU leaders in June.
